text: The Krimchi temples are a group of seven ancient Hindu temples situated in the Udhampur District of the Jammu Division in Jammu and Kashmir, India. Located on the bank of the Birunala stream in the village of Krimchi, the complex is 12 km from Udhampur and is locally known as the Pandava Temples. According to the Archaeological Survey of India, the temples were constructed between the 8th and 9th centuries AD, with construction occurring in stages; temples No. 6 and 7 are believed to have been damaged several centuries ago. Local tradition suggests the temples date back to the protagonists of the Mahabharata War or a late Pandava dynasty that ruled in Jammu and Kashmir, a theory proposed by Alexander Cunningham. Legend claims that Raja Kichak founded the town of Krimchi and the surrounding kingdom, and that the Pandavas during their exile stayed in the area for an extended period. Given their 8th-century construction, the temple complex reflects elements of Indo-Greek architecture. The complex includes four large and three small temples, with the main temple standing 50 feet tall and dedicated to Hindu deities such as Shiva, Ganesha, Vishnu, and Parvati. The architectural style is similar to classical Kashmiri temples in India. This article is a stub and can be expanded with additional information.
